source: Yoke Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (05-19-2026)

players.product: Precursors for memory (mainly DRAM) and advanced-logic fabs via UP Chemical (Korea) and Jiangsu Xianke (China), plus LDS liquid delivery systems

quarterly_data.quarter: Yoke Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (05-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chairman and general manager Shen Qi (2025 annual results briefing): the company already supplies products stably into its customers' HBM lines (customers not named in the answer); product volumes and prices are negotiated with customers at the start of each year, and a few products' prices can be raised with customers because of raw-material costs. Precursor capacity has not increased since the annual report; new capacity and products will be added as customer demand grows, customers keep qualifying its precursors and capacity will rise further in H2 2026. The Korean capacity serves large overseas customers and the Yixing capacity mainly domestic customers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Yoke Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (05-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Board secretary and CFO Qin Hongjian (2025 annual results briefing) on precursors: HBM precursors have been supplied continuously and demand keeps growing as domestic and overseas fabs add HBM capacity; silicon-based precursors face competition and price swings in China, while high-end precursors hold stable prices on high technical barriers and customer stickiness. Precursor shipments this year are up year on year and will rise as domestic memory customers ramp capacity; the precursor business is profitable, its sales have grown faster than the industry average, new precursors are being developed or introduced at customers and new metal-precursor capacity is being built. Domestic fabs' capacity is growing faster than overseas; semiconductor-materials revenue is roughly evenly split between domestic and overseas. Disclosed precursor capacity counts only lines that passed trial operation and were transferred to fixed assets; depreciation will rise with capacity but the company expects to maintain gross margin.

quarterly_data.quarter: Yoke Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (05-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Photoresists and packaging materials (2025 annual results briefing): chairman Shen Qi said the company is converting part of its TFT photoresist capacity to make advanced-packaging photoresists, including photoresists usable on glass substrates, and that low photoresist utilisation reflects the customer-introduction stage. CFO Qin Hongjian said its semiconductor precursors, semiconductor photoresists and ancillary reagents can all be used in the CoWoS packaging structure; semiconductor and packaging photoresists are in customer validation testing, with lines being built for products that have passed; display photoresists go mainly into LCD and also high-end OLED, with a leading domestic share (company claim).

quarterly_data.quarter: Yoke Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (05-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other businesses, CFO Qin Hongjian (2025 annual results briefing): LNG deliveries were lower in Q1 because of the Spring Festival and will rise in H2 as shipyard construction fills up, offshore being more than half of LNG revenue, and the company is confident of continued growth in 2026; electronic specialty gases (used in high-voltage electrical equipment and transmission and in semiconductor etching) are made in Chengdu and Inner Mongolia, with the Inner Mongolia plant planned to start trial production in Q3, and 2025 gas revenue fell mainly because of capacity limits, part of demand being served under OEM labelling; silica micro-powder is profitable and the Chengdu plant plans more capacity as chip-packaging and high-frequency high-speed CCL demand grows; wet electronic chemicals, whose customers include mainstream domestic and overseas wafer fabs and panel makers, add new capacity in H2.
